reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) directly supports the formation of (Hf,Zr)B2 precipitates, enhanced grain boundary cohesion, and improved ductility/work hardenability at room temperature, but provides no data on thermoelastic modulus or high-temperature (1273 K) behavior, leaving two key premises unsupported.
premises: Boron addition induces intergranular (Hf,Zr)B2 precipitates in HfMoNbTaTiZr
These precipitates enhance grain boundary cohesion
Enhanced cohesion improves ductility and work hardenability
Enhanced cohesion elevates the thermoelastic modulus
Effects are operative at high temperature (~1273 K)
